text:
Sam Bennett has two Stanley Cups and a Conn Smythe, so nobody in Florida is panicking over an October. Still, his season is a split picture. He has five goals in his last ten games, all of his scoring in that stretch, and he's shooting at volume again (43 shots in 17 games). The goals are earned: 3.6 expected goals from his own shots in those ten.

The odd part is everything around him. Florida controls play with him on, 55 percent of the expected goals at 5v5, yet his on-ice finishing is 4.41 goals below what those chances usually produce. That's why he has zero assists in ten games, and that is mostly bounces. His ice time has also slipped about two and a half minutes recently, which is worth watching.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season had him on the end of a lot of passes across the slot, the kind that go in 25 percent of the time. If his linemates start finishing, the assists pile up fast.
headline: Bennett's goals came back; the line hasn't
